title: No known physical law is transgressed by the bodily mechanism

fields.label: Label
fields.value: No known physical law is transgressed by the bodily mechanism

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: However complex living processes are, no physical law (including those of chemistry, surface action and osmosis) is known to be broken by the working of the body.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: But all the while, so far as I am aware, no physical law, any more than that of gravity itself, not even among the puzzles of chemical “stereometry,” or of physiological “surface-action” or “osmosis,” is known to be _transgressed_ by the bodily mechanism.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter I, “Introductory”; topic “Limits of physical explanation”. Scope: the physical and physiological mechanisms of all organisms

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch01-04: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.29

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Selected mechanisms can be checked against physical constraints, but the universal negative is not confirmable from datasets. Existing physiological records rarely include complete system boundaries needed for strong conservation tests.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Audit well-measured physiological processes for reproducible violations of conservation laws or established chemical and transport laws after closing their mass and energy budgets. A robust closed-system violation would refute the claim, but repeated compliance in sampled systems cannot confirm its unrestricted scope.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Apparent violations commonly reflect unmeasured fluxes or model error.

No finite dataset covers every organism and physical law.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Chemistry, surface action, and osmosis are specific enough that a quantitative violation in a well-measured system would count against the claim, and tabulated biophysical numbers exist for those checks. The scope is still all bodily mechanisms of all organisms, the phrase about what is known tracks the literature rather than a dataset, and consistency is weak evidence against a rival that allows rare exceptions. A small team could audit a few laws, not the universal claim.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For named classes of law, compare measured osmotic equilibria, surface stresses, and chemical stoichiometry in cells and tissues with the values ordinary physics requires. A systematic, replicated violation would refute the claim for that law; agreement in a studied system would support only that restricted case.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Agreement in model cells does not rule out a subtle non-physical contribution elsewhere.

The claim is an open-ended negative over every law and every organism.
